themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 83 this week versus a baseline of 20.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 300% increase—suggesting a potential new source of sustained disruption or event-related activity in East Harlem.
evidence: 83 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 20.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.72)
300% spike from baseline represents statistically significant anomaly
Community board has repeatedly requested traffic enforcement agents, suggesting ongoing noise/congestion concerns
reporting_angles: What new construction, event, or commercial activity triggered this spike? Interview residents on specific blocks.
Are recent 125th Street rezoning/development applications (58-62 E. 125th, 132 E. 125th) driving increased truck traffic or street activity?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 9 this week against a baseline of 2.1 per week—a 324% increase—marking an acute emergence of open-air drug market or use concerns in East Harlem this week.
evidence: 9 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.73)
324% spike indicates new or intensified street-level drug activity
Aligns temporally with April 6 NYPD police shooting incident (knife-wielding man outside East Harlem grocery store), suggesting broader public safety volatility
reporting_angles: Canvass residents and merchants on which blocks/corners are seeing open-air drug sales; has encampment growth (see below) created new vending sites?
Interview NYPD about whether recent shooting and drug spike are connected or reflect broader disorder in specific neighborhoods.

themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints more than quintupled last week to 14 versus a baseline of 2.4 per week—a 490% increase—signaling a rapid expansion of street homelessness or unsanctioned encampments in East Harlem.
evidence: 14 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.46)
490% spike indicates rapid emergence or visible concentration of encampments
Community board budget requests include public health issue programs (DOHMH), but no recent funding increases visible
reporting_angles: Where are the new encampments forming? Map by block and interview homeless service providers about whether shelters are at capacity or whether new populations are arriving.
Interview residents and merchants on safety, sanitation, and service demands created by encampment growth; connect to unsanitary condition complaints (830 total in 90 days).

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1500% spike—indicating either a coordinated tagging campaign or emergence of gang-related vandalism in East Harlem this week.
evidence: 4 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66)
Community board has repeatedly requested graffiti removal/cleaning increases from Department of Sanitation, suggesting chronic underlying problem
reporting_angles: Investigate whether graffiti is gang-related tagging, political/protest messaging, or isolated vandalism; interview NYPD and local business owners.
Cross-check with police reports and gang intelligence units to see if this correlates with turf disputes or new crew activity in the district.

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints doubled to 20 last week versus a baseline of 6.4 per week—a 214% increase—suggesting either a coordinated wave of construction projects or persistent building code violations in East Harlem.
evidence: 20 general construction/plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.4 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.82)
214% spike coincides with 542 DOB permits filed (447 alterations) in last 90 days, suggesting active construction environment
Heat/hot water complaints remain the top issue at 3788 over 90 days, often linked to aging building systems and inadequate maintenance
reporting_angles: Which DOB permit-holders or projects are generating the most complaints? Cross-reference construction permits with 311 complaint addresses.
Interview building inspectors about whether the spike reflects legitimate renovation work or unlicensed work/code violations in rent-stabilized housing.
